data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same files (PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO) and agreed the PKGBUILD is safe with standard practices: pinned GitHub release source, SHA-256 checksum verification, standard meson build process, no suspicious network operations or obfuscated code. The disagreement arose solely because the first model (qwen3-235b) encountered an API error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The second model (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed .SRCINFO and correctly identified it as benign metadata with no executable content. Since .SRCINFO is purely declarative metadata and cannot execute code, and both models found the PKGBUILD safe with proper source pinning and checksums, the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (API failure) in the first model when reviewing .SRCINFO, not by a genuine security concern. The first model correctly assessed the PKGBUILD as safe but could not complete the .SRCINFO review due to an HTTP 400 error. The second model successfully reviewed both files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: First model (qwen3-235b) failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should not result in inconclusive verdicts when other models have successfully reviewed the same files and found them safe, especially for non-executable files like .SRCINFO
When multiple models agree on the safety of executable files (PKGBUILD) and only disagree due to tool errors on metadata files, the consensus on executable files should drive the verdict
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for API errors to prevent incomplete audits from triggering unnecessary escalations
